what: The header of the prompt corpus published as an API: the version a project freezes. Declared BY HAND, for the same reason as the gate catalogue (gates/catalog.json): a project starts and finishes with the same version of the method, so what it froze has to read back the same two years from now.

version_scheme.note: The recipe -- canonical form, algorithm, encoding, and the rule that raises the version -- is declared once, there, and the build uses the same implementation. This file only says which keys the hash covers here, because the payload is a different one. One copy of each text.
version_scheme.what_is_covered: `what` is covered by the fingerprint (since corpus_version 2026.10.4). It is the key where the file states what it is and what travels verbatim, so a frozen copy altered there would misdescribe itself and the recomputed hash would still match. The same reasoning covers `counts` in the gate catalogue.

changelog.changed: First DECLARED version of the corpus. The prompts themselves did not change: not one character of prompt text is touched here (D-049). What changes is the identity of what is published and the truth of what it declares. Identity: until now the only identifier was a git sha, which a build computes before saving and which therefore always names the change BEFORE the one that contains it -- useless as something to freeze. From here the version is declared by hand and the file carries a content hash the consumer RECOMPUTES, exactly like the gate catalogue. Truth: the file said language `en` while steps[].title carried the Spanish titles of the contracts; the titles now come from the English contracts (docs/en/peldanos/), which is where tool data belongs (D-051), so the declaration is true instead of approximately true. The file stays UTF-8 and is not ASCII: the prompt text is published verbatim, typographic punctuation included.

One prompt changed, and it is the first time the published corpus changes a prompt instead of its identity. The step 2 prompt now also asks for the two prior inputs of Annex H -- the user glossary, with the words people actually use for each thing, and the list of profiles, saying who each one is and what they come to do -- taken from the survey, asked for rather than invented, written as files of the project and named from the project file. The gate data already demanded both at step 2 (the two prior-input anchors, since_schema 2) and the contract did not ask for them: the asymmetry between the published data and the prose is what the step 23 retrospective found, and it is what step 11 hunts. The English piece is one piece, identical byte for byte in the eight versions, and build/prompts.mjs enforces that; the translation of the prompt was written in each of the seven. No other prompt moved.

The same step 2 prompt changes again, and for the second half of the same finding. Yesterday it started asking for the two prior inputs of Annex H and left their file names to the project, because the owner had not declared any; today the owner declared them, so the prompt names them: the glossary goes to docs/GLOSSARY.md and the list of profiles to docs/PROFILES.md, and the two are named from the project file as before. It matters that the prompt says it and not only the gate data: an artifact the gate looks for by path and the prompt does not name is a gate that fails for a reason the person was never told. The English piece is one piece, identical in the eight versions, and build/prompts.mjs enforces that; the reader-facing translation was rewritten in each of the seven. No other prompt moved.

No prompt moved. What moved is the identity of the file and two sentences about it. `what` is now COVERED by the fingerprint: it is the key where the file says what it is and what travels verbatim, so a frozen copy altered there would misdescribe itself while the recomputed hash still matched. And the two sentences that said the English piece is identical in `the eight versions` no longer carry a count: they point at the list the method declares once, in the gate catalogue under `languages.prose_versions`. The corpus is the same 54 prompts in the same 24 contracts.

Every prompt of the corpus carries one clause more, and it is the same clause: the form of the question. The method ordered the model to ASK twenty-two times, in fifteen of the twenty-seven files, and never said HOW. Now each of the seventy-two prompts closes with the four parts of UX-28 -- the data that makes the question necessary, listed; one paragraph of no more than five lines that links it and lets the question be seen; the question with its possible answers numbered; the recommendation -- and with the depth parameter project_config.communication_depth (beginner, decision_maker, technical; undeclared means decision_maker). It is one single English wording, identical in the eight prose versions the method declares, which is the rule that already governed every prompt and is what build/prompts.mjs verifies byte by byte. Nothing else moved: no prompt lost a sentence and no prompt changed its order. This is the written exception to D-044 and it is narrow -- the clause names the four parts and the parameter and nothing else, the full statement lives once in Annex H -- because unlike the other forty-five rules this one is a demand on the conversation and not on the artifact, so the only place it can be obeyed from is what the model reads (D-070, PND-054).

Not one character of prompt text is touched. `what` now carries, in one single copy shared with the gate catalogue and with the index of the data interface, the SCOPE of what the content hash protects: it is self-consistent, so whoever can edit a file can recompute it; it detects truncation, a bad merge and hand editing; it does not protect against an adversary who controls the host that served the file; the anchors that do not live on that host are the version ledger and the transport security; and there is no cryptographic signature, which is a written decision with its cost on the table and not an oversight. That sentence had lived since 2026.10.2 only in the index, which carries no hash of its own by design (D-056), so it travelled unprotected -- and a security declaration in an unprotected field is one an attacker can edit to say the opposite. It could only move into the resources once `what` was covered by the hash, which happened for this corpus in 2026.10.4. This version also gets an address of its own that returns it and only it, with no purge, declared by the index (D-073, PND-008, PND-009).

The working agreement goes from six minimum rules to eight, and the five rules of the inherited path are renumbered from (7)..(11) to (9)..(13). The two new ones are the conduct side of the two rules D-078 added to Annex H: (7) every figure the agent hands the owner comes with its receipt -- what it counted, how many it expected to count, what it depended on and what it reports when it could not look --, and (8) a command presented as read-only runs without permission to write and a check that exercises a destructive operation runs where its statement cannot land, so that nothing having changed is measured and not promised. Why this does not break D-044, which forbids copying the statement of a rule into a prompt: these two are not that statement. Annex H demands the receipt of the INSTRUMENTS OF THE SYSTEM, measured over artifacts; the working agreement demands it of what the AGENT HANDS THE OWNER in the conversation, which is the same distinction that made UX-28 the written exception (D-070) -- and the six rules of the agreement were never annex rules to begin with. The contract of step 1 says so in its own prose, in the eight languages, so that nobody reads the pair as a second copy of the annex. Measured while doing it, and reported as a finding of its own: the Chinese translation of the inherited-path prompt numbered its five legacy rules 8, 11, 7, 12, 13 -- out of order, with two numbers that did not exist in any other language -- since before this change; the renumbering leaves all eight languages with 9 to 13 in order. The English piece stays byte-identical in the sixteen copies that carry it (eight contracts and eight copies in the course manual), which build/prompts.mjs demands (D-078, PND-065 to PND-068). Rule (7) was SCOPED before this version was ever served, which is why the correction lives in this same entry and does not open a new one: a version nobody could ask for is worse than a corrected one (same reading as the gate catalogue of 2026.10.7, D-069). The first wording demanded a receipt for EVERY figure the agent hands the owner, which is more than Annex H demands of an instrument -- "every instrument the project decides with" -- and more than the line four rows below it, which says the receipt of the instrument is owed each time a figure decides something. A conversation carries dozens of figures that decide nothing -- how many files were touched, how many seconds it took -- so a rule that demands a receipt for all of them is broken on day one, which is what the alarm of step 1 warns about, and it left the reader choosing between two wordings of the same method. Rule (7) now reads "every figure you hand me that a decision rests on". How it was found belongs to the subject: by comparing the THREE wordings of the same rule, not by reading one -- each of the three reads fine alone -- which is the cross-check of PND-083 applied inside a single language (D-078, PND-083).

The prompts of steps 12, 13 and 23 gain what the two decisions of 2026-11-02 ask a control to carry when it closes (D-079, D-080). Step 13: the report declares, under the fixed key auditor_choice, which case applies and who decided it -- different_model, same_model_declared or tool_constraint -- and names in its Auditor: line the model that built and the model that audits; it audits the health of the register of the evidence as a dimension that is not optional, under evidence_register_health, with each figure measured by a program and with the command next to it, and a figure it could not measure declared as not measured and never as zero; and it closes with findings_by_destination, every finding assigned to product, method or tool, with the register where its pending item goes. The closing prompt, the one that goes to the builder, opens each pending item in the register of the destination the report assigned to it and asks the owner before opening anything when a finding arrives with none. Steps 12 and 23 gain the same closing by destination, which is what makes the immunisation of the method a mechanism instead of somebody remembering. The English piece is one and identical in the eight languages, as always (D-013), and each version carries its translated block; the clauses enter as a paragraph of their own immediately before the UX-28 clause, so nothing already written was rewritten and the closing sentence stays last. The keys travel in English even when the report is in the language of the reader, which is D-075 applied to a document of a project: a key that a gate reads is a key. What this version does NOT do: touch the prompt of any other step, or the lessons of the course, whose step-13 prompt is a shorter teaching version that no guard compares against the contract -- that is registered as a finding of the method and not fixed here.

The prompts of steps 10 and 13 gain what the two decisions of 2026-11-02 ask of a step whose work is done outside (D-081, D-082). Step 13: the report declares its own completeness under audit_completeness, with findings_announced and findings_written carrying their figures and having to be the same figure, and with the instruction not to announce a count it is not going to write and not to stop halfway and emit a closing marker as if it had finished; the grade of each audited dimension under dimension_grades; the verdict of each receipt it reran under receipts_reproduced, at least one, because a receipt that was only read is not one of them; and what it did not audit under not_audited, part by part and with the pending item that is open for it, since an audit with a smaller scope declared up front is worth more than a wide one with holes. Step 10: the file of manual cases carries at its head cases_written, cases_executed_by_a_person -- moved only by a signed execution and never by the reading of the agent -- and execution_debt with who owes which execution and since when, a debt that is not a gate of its own because what the step asks for is the declaration and not a figure above zero, and that is never silent either; and the agent walks the screens itself, which is a different thing from the execution a person owes and never a replacement for it, writing a file of its own with the number of screens the system has, how many were walked and how many defects came out, where a screen that could not be reached is counted inside the total with its reason. The closing prompt of the execution refreshes the figures from the signed tables and from nothing else. The English piece is one and identical in the eight languages, as always (D-013), and each version carries its translated block; the clauses enter as paragraphs of their own immediately before the UX-28 clause, so nothing already written was rewritten and the closing sentence stays last. What this version does NOT do: touch the prompt of any other step, or the lessons of the course, whose prompts are a shorter teaching version that no guard compares against the contract -- that is registered as a finding of the method and not fixed here.

The prompt of step 9 gains the column the compliance documents did not have (D-084). docs/CODE_QUALITY.md and docs/USABILITY.md declare at their head criteria_total -- counting the rules nobody has verified yet, which is the denominator CQ-19.1 asks of any instrument --, criteria_verified_by_a_program with the command next to the figure, criteria_verified_by_a_person signed with a name and a date, and verification_debt with who owes each verification and since when; and then, criterion by criterion, verified_by with the instrument the catalogue ALREADY declares for that rule -- auto_gate, matrix_query, e2e_per_profile or manual_case -- read from the data and never chosen by the agent, because the data has said since it exists that a manual_case is judged by a person and returns passed or failed with a name and a date. And the rule the clause exists for: a criterion whose instrument is manual_case and carries no signature is written not_verifiable and never as met, because a criterion a person has to judge and nobody judged is a criterion waiting for its person and has to read that way. It was measured and not supposed: in the cycle of 2026-11-02 a compliance document had to be corrected and six criteria went from verified to not verifiable, one single one staying verified, because the verifier of the others was a person who never executed the cases -- and the agent had not lied, the document had nowhere to say whose the criterion was. The English piece is one and identical in the eight languages, as always (D-013), and each version carries its translated block; the clause enters as a paragraph of its own immediately before the UX-28 clause, so nothing already written was rewritten and the closing sentence stays last. The keys travel in English even when the document is in the language of the reader, which is D-075 applied to a document of a project: a key that a gate reads is a key. What this version does NOT do: touch the prompt of any other step -- step 10 gained its answer in the prose of its contract and not in its prompt, because what was missing there was not an instruction to the agent but an answer to the owner (D-083) --, and touch the prompts of the course manuals, which are a shorter teaching version whose divergence is declared and guarded from D-085 on, in the prose of the method and not in this corpus.
